finding: Backtest does not test the published score: in 5 of 6 folds the D30 guard drops S as well as I and H, so the fold 'score' is consistency (C) alone, with massive ties; top-10 membership is then an arbitrary tie-break
evidence: Re-ran every fold: informative flags {S,I,H,C} = bat2024 {T,F,F,T}; bat2025, bat2026, bowl2024, bowl2025, bowl2026 all {F,F,F,T} (S k ~3e12). Distinct score values per fold: bat 17/5/9, bowl 2/6/10 (of 17/35/58 and 39/62/76 players). Bowl 2024: 2 distinct scores, 0 players strictly above the 10th, 18 tied at the cut. Bowl 2025: 3 strictly above, 12 tied for 7 slots. topk() uses sort_values quicksort so ties follow index order. 2024 fold history is one season, so c_n=1 for all players (C is binary). Randomising ties 5,000 times gives pooled hit rate bowlers 59.1% (range 38.9-83.3, 5-95% 50.0-69.2) and batters 59.9% (53.3-64.3) versus reported 64.7 / 57.1. Using the weights the checkpoint says were effective (2/3 S + 1/3 C, S not dropped) gives batters 50.0% (n=16) and bowlers 52.6% (n=19) vs naive 50.0 / 84.2. Checkpoint 4 and D30 never mention this; D30 says only I and H are inert
suggested_fix: Replace the binary informative/zero guard with a continuous rule so S is never silently dropped (e.g. cap k, or z = (posterior mean - mu)/sqrt(between variance) instead of re-standardising shrunken values). Break ties explicitly (by raw S, or random with fixed seed) and report the number of distinct scores and tied players per fold. Re-run the backtest and report old and new numbers side by side, with the tie-break distribution

finding: D30 is a deviation from the frozen spec but is labelled a faithful implementation; checkpoint says 'score exactly as pre-registered' while effective weights are S 2/3, C 1/3 (and C 100% in most backtest folds). It was made after the backtest was run, and it moved the bowler backtest from 47.4% to 64.7%
evidence: D29 says any later change must be logged as a deviation and reported both ways. Spec section 4 weights are 0.40/0.25/0.15/0.20 with no rule that zeroes a component; D30 says 'The spec is unchanged'. Checkpoint 4 line 1: 'score exactly as pre-registered'. D30 itself says the pre-fix backtest existed (step4_backtest_summary_prefix_bug.csv) before the fix, so D16/D5 (no feedback from backtest to the metric) are not demonstrably met. Only the backtest is reported both ways; the pre-fix leaderboard was not kept. I recomputed it: literal spec top-10 overlaps D30 top-10 by 9/10 for batters and 9/10 for bowlers (Spearman 0.98/0.96), so the main board barely moves, yet bowler hit rate moved 17 points, which shows how noisy the backtest is (see separate finding)
suggested_fix: Log D30 as a deviation, not a faithful implementation; reword Checkpoint 4 ('effective weights S 2/3, C 1/3 on the final board; backtest folds differ, see table'); archive the pre-fix leaderboards and report top-10 and top-20 overlap pre vs post; state in D30 the order of events (fix versus backtest)

finding: D30 guard is a fragile binary cliff caused by re-standardising shrunken components; its outcome depends on a noise estimate that is itself biased
evidence: Noise term uses recency-weighted n as the precision (v_noise = mean(sigma2/n_w)). The variance of a recency-weighted mean is sigma2*sum(w^2 n)/(sum(w n))^2, which is smaller. With that correction batter I flips to between-variance +2.4e-7 (informative, k about 11,600) and bowler S rises from 0.0029 to 0.0111 (k from 1,101 to about 290). Main-board bowler S is only barely 'informative' (v_obs/v_noise = 1.09; batters 1.45). Because every component is z-scored after shrinkage, a component with near-zero reliability gets full weight the moment its estimated between-variance is positive, and zero the moment it is not. Pre-fix I ranked players by n x excess, as D30 says
suggested_fix: Standardise by the estimated between-player sd (so low-reliability components get proportionally low weight) rather than the sd of shrunken values; use effective sample size sum(w n)^2/sum(w^2 n) in the noise term; remove the hard switch

finding: D30 substance checked and holds: I (WPA per ball) and H (pressure drop) have no detectable between-player signal. But H's within-variance formula is wrong
evidence: Independent split-half test (random halves of each player's matches, 200 repeats, scorable batters 45 / bowlers 71): correlation of halves S 0.30/0.11, I 0.004/-0.04, H 0.002/-0.07 (batters/bowlers). So the conclusion is not an artefact. H bug: code uses (var_hi+var_lo)/nH with nH = n_hi*n_lo/(n_hi+n_lo), which doubles the noise; correct is var_hi/n_hi + var_lo/n_lo. Noise used 0.0835 (bat) and 0.0908 (bowl) vs correct 0.0422 and 0.0459; observed variance 0.0368 and 0.0321, so between-variance is -0.0054 and -0.0138 even after correction. Conclusion unchanged, code wrong
suggested_fix: Fix the H noise formula (var_hi/n_hi + var_lo/n_lo per player) and re-run; keep a split-half reliability table in the outputs as the evidence for dropping I and H

finding: Bowler leaderboard is barely informative and the checkpoint does not say so; intervals show top-10 bowlers cannot be separated
evidence: Bowler S: observed/noise variance 1.09, EB k = 1,101 balls, shrunken S range -0.044..0.036 versus raw -0.63..0.36; split-half reliability r = 0.11 (Spearman-Brown 0.20). Top-10 bowler pairs with non-overlapping 80% intervals: 0 of 45 (batters 8 of 45). 17 of 71 bowler intervals exclude 50. Rank-1 batter interval is very narrow (98.7-99.99) because Phi saturates: the score is not a percentile. Checkpoint 4 presents ranks without this caveat; 'too close to call' (spec section 2) is not produced anywhere
suggested_fix: State plainly in the checkpoint that bowler differences are mostly noise at these sample sizes; output a too-close-to-call flag per pair or tier; do not describe the 0-100 score as a percentile

finding: Backtest headline claims outrun the evidence
evidence: Pooled score top-10 'assessable' sample is 14 batters and 17 bowlers (naive 16 / 19); 16 of 30 batter slots and 13 of 30 bowler slots are non-assessable; counting them as misses gives 26.7 / 36.7% vs naive 26.7 / 53.3%. Base rate (share of all assessable qualifiers above average) is 51.8% batters and 56.8% bowlers, so batter 57.1% is indistinguishable from picking at random; this base rate is not reported. Same 19/18 distinct players fill 30 slots, so folds are not independent. Checkpoint says 'naive economy predicts better' for bowlers; the pre-registered wording is 'persistence not demonstrated', and an 80% interval on ~18 players that also depends on tie-breaks does not support the stronger claim. The 17-point swing (47.4 to 64.7) from a re-ranking that changes 1 of 10 names is the best evidence the hit rate is noise
suggested_fix: Report base rate, counts (hits/n), distinct players and the as-miss rate next to each hit rate; use the pre-registered wording; present both score and naive as 'cannot be distinguished from base rate' unless interval and tie robustness say otherwise

finding: Batter dismissals undercounted, so average and balls per dismissal are wrong for some players
evidence: outs are built only from balls faced (wides excluded) plus non-striker rows selected by wpa_nonstriker_out != 0. (a) 20 dismissals fall on wides (14 stumped, 6 run out; 18 are the striker), 7 of them High; striker ones not counted. (b) 16 non-striker run-outs all on the last ball of an innings have wpa_nonstriker_out = 0 and are dropped (13 of them High). Net: 19 High dismissals missing across 17 in-scope batters versus a direct count of is_wicket & player_out_id == player. Examples (step3_batting_metrics): Abdul Samad High_avg 49.75, true 33.17 (outs 4 vs 6); Krunal Pandya 51.0 vs 40.8; Kuldeep Yadav 9.0 vs 5.4; Sanju Samson 34.1 vs 30.3. Definitions say dismissals are charged to the player out. Affects descriptive avg/balls per out only, not the score
suggested_fix: Count outs as wicket rows with player_out_id == player (exclude retired-not-out), independent of ball_faced and WPA; re-run Step 3 tables

finding: Sensitivity result is vacuous after D30
evidence: I and H weights are inert, so 8 of the 16 +/-10% cases cannot change anything; S/C changes give 100% top-10 overlap in all 16 cases. Checkpoint reports 'keeps 100%' as reassurance. A coarse alternative shows the board does depend on weights: S 30% / C 70% gives top-10 overlap 6/10 batters, 8/10 bowlers; C-only 6/8; S-only 9/10
suggested_fix: Say the +/-10% test is uninformative after D30; add an alternative-weights table (S-only, C-only, equal) as a clearly labelled extra

finding: Backtest bootstrap of hit-rate difference is approximate
evidence: d.sample(replace=True).drop_duplicates shrinks the resampled pool to about 63% of players, ties are broken randomly inside the bootstrap but by index order in the point estimate, and players repeated across folds are treated as independent. Interval not centred on the point estimate (bowlers point -19.5, interval -25.0 to -3.3; batters +7.1, -11.5 to +10.0)
suggested_fix: Resample players with replacement keeping duplicates as weights (or resample matches), apply the same tie rule as the point estimate, and cluster by player across folds

finding: Pre-registered sensitivity output incomplete: top-10 overlap for strict-D18 and season-centred variants missing
evidence: Spec section 5: 'Report the top-10 and top-20 overlap for each'. step4_definition_robustness.csv has only top20_overlap_pct and spearman_common. Checkpoint 4 also reports top-20 only
suggested_fix: Add top10_overlap_pct for every variant

finding: Bowler 'death economy' is not High-pressure as pre-registered
evidence: Section 3: all metrics are on High-pressure balls unless stated. Code computes death_econ_all over all pressure levels (g[g.phase=='Death']); the High-pressure death figure exists only as High_rse_per100_death. Boundary % conceded uses deliveries as denominator while dot % uses legal balls
suggested_fix: Add High-pressure death economy, rename or drop death_econ_all, use one denominator for boundary and dot

finding: All-rounder combined impact and interval deviate from the spec
evidence: Combined WPA sums batting+bowling WPA over all pressure levels (not High) and divides by max(bat_matches, bowl_matches) not distinct matches (Jadeja 54 vs 55 union; High-only per match 0.0109 vs table 0.0106). Interval is the average of the batting and bowling bounds, not a joint match bootstrap; averaging independent bounds is wider than the true interval of the average
suggested_fix: State the weighting and bucket; use distinct matches; bootstrap bat and bowl jointly by match

finding: EB prior mean and C prior mean differ slightly from the spec text
evidence: Spec: mu is the mean among scorable players. Code uses the mean weighted by recency-weighted n (_eb: np.average(..., weights=n)); C prior is pooled seasons-positive over pooled seasons, not the mean of player shares. Effect not quantified (suspected small)
suggested_fix: Document as a deviation or use the unweighted mean

finding: Step 3 tables have no 80% intervals or minimum samples for descriptive splits
evidence: Master STEP 3 asks for 80% intervals on every ranked metric. step3_*_metrics.csv hold point values only for all 232 batters and 177 bowlers in scope; mean High balls in the spin split is 15.8, pace 35.5, death 19.6, setting 12.5. Intervals exist only for the score and raw S
suggested_fix: Add sample columns with a suppression threshold, or intervals, for splits; label splits below a minimum as too small

finding: Consistency benchmark is zero, not the league mean
evidence: C counts seasons with RAE/RSE per ball > 0. League High mean is +0.039 (batters) and -0.041 (bowlers), season offsets +0.004..+0.040 (D28), so >0 is easy for batters and strict for bowlers (prior C 0.565 vs 0.493). The backtest outcome uses 'above the season league mean', a different benchmark
suggested_fix: Use season-mean-relative C in a labelled variant, or state the asymmetry as a limitation

finding: Bowler RSE per delivery gives wides a positive credit
evidence: In High balls the mean RSE on a wide is +0.374 (wides are 4.5% of High deliveries), on legal balls -0.053, on no-balls -1.65. S uses all deliveries. Effect on ranking small (Spearman 0.975 versus S without wides), upstream in Step 2
suggested_fix: Charge the re-bowl cost to wides or compute S on legal balls; note in Step 2 limitations

finding: Batter WPA is zero on every wide, including 20 wides with a wicket, while the bowler is credited
evidence: wpa_batter != 0 on 0 of 2,790 wides; wpa_bowler != 0 on all of them. Stumpings and run-outs of the striker on wides give the bowler +0.03..+0.15 and the batter 0
suggested_fix: Assign the batter's side of the WPA on wide dismissals; log as a limitation

finding: Scope silently excludes 2 players seen in raw 2025-26 data
